title: Burst preemption zones and headroom budgets for continuous batching
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: during bursty traffic windows continuous batching increases token throughput but requires transient GPU memory headroom for KV shards and activation spikes. We observe tail latency spikes and a small number of OOMs when multiple multi-model requests with long seq lengths overlap. Proposed solution: introduce fine-grained preemption zones (preemptible memory slabs) and an explicit burst headroom budgeting mechanism per-GPU that differentiates weights (pinned), hot-KV slices (low-cost eviction), and activations (preemptible/offloadable). The system will compute a live headroom budget using sequence-length-aware request forecasting and assign labeled preemption zones that can be reclaimed on short notices with controlled degrade policies (drop to smaller KV shard, offload activations to CPU/pmem, or throttle admission). This ticket covers design, telemetry, prototype implementation, and a staged rollout (canary -> fleet).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-GPU headroom gauge and preemption-zone occupancy metrics in the console dashboard
Under synthetic burst tests (2x baseline qps for 30s) tail p99 latency improves by >=20% compared to baseline without preemption zones
No increase in OOM incident rate in canary fleet; successful fallback to activation offload or KV eviction within configured reclaim latency (<=35ms median)
Canary rollout config and automation scripts exist (k8s feature flag + rollout policy) and documented runbook for manual rollback
comments: 2025-02-14 Priya Nair: Created ticket after postmortem of 2025-02-10 OOM cluster incident. Attached preliminary mem profiling and seq-length heatmap.

2025-02-15 Diego Martinez: Spike analysis shows KV hot-slices account for ~28% of transient allocations during bursts; activations responsible for ~45%. Propose allocating separate small preemptible slab for activations to enable fast offload.

2025-02-16 Tomislav Novak (review): Concern about fragmentation if we use static slab sizes. Recommend a hybrid: slab buckets with fallback to ephemeral frames and a compacting reclamation pass during low load.

2025-02-17 Aisha Khan (Perf): Ran microbench harness. Prototype reclaim path (evict-hot-kv->offload-activations) adds ~12ms median on reclaim but reduces p99 latency by 30% during bursts. We'll need kernel-level coalescing to avoid repeated small evictions.

2025-02-18 Diego Martinez: Implementing telemetry hooks: per-allocation tags (weight|kv_hot|kv_cold|activation_ephemeral) + reclaim counters. Preparing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1234

2025-02-19 Morgan Lee (PM): Ensure rollout has tenant-level controls and opt-out for Dedicated customers. Documenting policy options in the proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SERV/Burst+Preemption+Zones

2025-02-20 Priya Nair: Added canary config for runtime-1.20: preemption_zone_size_pct default 8%, reclaim_threshold=0.88, activation_offload_target=cpu. Observability dashboard draft: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/memory/preemption-zones
impact_analysis: Memory model: weights pinned ~60% of GPU resident footprint for large models; KV hot slices + activations share remaining 40% but are highly bursty.
Headroom budget heuristic: base_headroom = max(0.06 * gpu_total, 1GB) + quantile(seq_len,0.95)*avg_activation_per_token*expected_concurrent_requests

Risk: aggressive preemption may increase token latency for affected requests; mitigations include progressive reclaim priorities and tenant-aware QoS (protected tenants with SLA will have lower preemptible allocation).
Cost: additional CPU/network I/O for activation offload estimated +5% infra cost at peak for worst-case bursts, acceptable vs. p99 latency regressions observed today.
experiments: A: Static preemption slab 8% of GPU vs B: adaptive headroom based on 95th seq — measure p99 and OOMs
Measure reclaim latency distribution and correlated p99 gen latency across 5 model families (llama-2-13b, redwood-7b, transformer-xl variants)
A/B tenant test: opt-in Dedicated tenants to validate behavior and gather customer impact feedback
rollout_plan: 1) Merge telemetry + flags behind feature gate (runtime-1.20).
2) Internal canary (5% capacity) with synthetic burst tests + chaos scenarios (node reboots, network flaps).
3) Gradual ramp to 30% with monitoring thresholds for auto-rollback if OOMs or latency regressions exceed SLA.
4) Enterprise opt-in and documentation + support playbook.
notes: Consider integrating with existing KV tiering code (ENG-53921) to avoid duplicate eviction logic.
Follow-up ticket: expose tenant-level preemption policy and billing signals (P0 candidate if early customers request).
